summary: Waren Spacefarer, a young pilot, wants forty thousand credits to buy Marta Okafor's Kestrel. He exposed Dren Vasko's people smuggling and filed an informant claim, but it pays out months from now. He flew Juno Reyes's medicine run to Occator Ridge and owned up to the broken strut, so Juno paid him in full. He took the Halcyon salvage job, which pays forty-five thousand for the recorder and nav core, minus Juno's ten percent. In her salvage skiff he scanned the tumbling wreck. The recorder bay hatch is buckled and will need cutting. A loose hull plate sweeps past the bay a few seconds behind it, and the nav core sits near the break.

facts: Marta Okafor will sell the Kestrel to Waren for forty thousand credits.
Vasko promised Waren six hundred credits on delivery to Vesta.
Waren killed the Grubstake's main drive breaker; the tug can't burn.
Vasko surrendered and wants customs told it was all his doing.
Eleven refugees from the Grubstake hold are now in customs custody.
A customs informant fund pays only after a statement, a conviction and a review, months away.
Waren filed an informant fund claim; any payout is months away.
The refugee woman with the toddler asked for Waren's name.
The ridge pad approach: come in low from the north, mind the hab mast at forty metres.
The Halcyon's insurer pays forty-five thousand for her flight recorder and nav core.
Juno's last pilot on the Halcyon run lost his skiff but survived.
Waren flies Juno's borrowed salvage skiff and must bring it back.
The Halcyon's aft section swings past every eleven seconds.
The Halcyon's recorder hatch is buckled; a loose hull plate sweeps past seconds after it.

recent.narration:
The skiff leaps off the ring, and Ceres swells grey beneath you. You come in from the north, low, and pass the hab mast with room to spare. Then the dust rises like a curtain, and your sensors go blank.

You fly by eye. For a moment it's perfect. Then a pocket of loose regolith slides under the port pad, and the skiff drops a hand's width onto the starboard strut.

The weld cracks. The damper bursts with a shriek. The skiff lurches sideways and your ribs slam into the harness as the starboard side sags toward the edge of the ledge. Beyond it is nothing but crater shadow.

The engines are still idling and the crate is still strapped in behind you. Through the dust, figures in pressure suits are running from the hab lock.
recent.picture: A stubby courier skiff with a scarred belly tilting dangerously on a narrow landing ledge jutting from a grey crater wall on Ceres, broken starboard landing strut, grey dust swirling, black starry sky. Inside the cockpit a lean young man in his early twenties, short dark brown hair, light stubble, keen grey eyes, worn olive flight jacket over a grey t-shirt, grips the controls. Distant figures in pressure suits run from a hab airlock.

recent.action: Radio the hab crew for anchors
recent.narration:
You key the open channel and keep your voice flat. "Skiff on the pad, starboard strut gone. I need anchors on the port side, now. Nobody near the starboard edge."

A gravelly voice answers. "Copy, pilot. Hold her steady." Three suited figures crouch low and haul cable from the hab lock. They spike two ground anchors into the rock and snap the lines onto your port tie-downs. The cables go taut and the skiff groans, then settles. It's crooked, but it's not going anywhere.

You kill the engines. Your hands are shaking now that they're allowed to.

The crew unloads the white crate and hurries it inside. A minute later your comm blinks. It's Bay Nine, Juno Reyes, and she has already seen the telemetry.

recent.action: Answer Juno and own the strut
recent.narration:
"Juno. The strut's on me. Loose regolith slid under the port pad, and I put her down a hand's width too hard. The medicine's inside, though, and nothing else is bent."

The line goes quiet. Then a short laugh. "The last guy told me the pad moved. You're the first one who didn't lie." The comm pings: three hundred credits, all of it. "I'm sending a crawler with a spare strut. You'll fly her home tomorrow."

She pauses. "Listen. The ridge hab wants a contract pilot who can put down on that ledge every week. It's steady money. There's also a bigger job I don't take, a salvage run in the deep belt. It pays like a ship. Interested?"

recent.action: Ask about the deep belt salvage run
recent.narration:
"Tell me about the salvage run."

Juno exhales. "There's an ore freighter called the Halcyon. She broke up three months ago in a rock field out in the deep belt. Her insurer will pay forty-five thousand to whoever brings back her flight recorder and nav core. They want to know whether it was the crew or the ship."

"Why don't you take it?"

"Because the wreck is still tumbling, and the field around it is full of her own debris. I sent a pilot out there in the spring. He came home, but his skiff didn't." Her voice stays even. "I'll lend you a salvage skiff. The insurer pays you and I take ten percent. You'd leave once the strut's fixed."

After her cut, that's the Kestrel.

recent.action: Take the Halcyon job, no hesitation
recent.narration:
"I'll take it." Juno doesn't argue. "Then get some sleep, Spacefarer."

You sleep on a cot in the ridge hab. By morning the crawler has come and gone, and the new strut holds when you lift off. At Bay Nine, Juno hands you the codes to a battered salvage skiff with grapples and a cutting arm. "Bring the skiff back. The money's nice too."

Two days out, the deep belt is dark and quiet. Then the Halcyon slides into your forward view. She's broken in half and tumbling slowly, with glittering debris all around her. The recorder bay is on the aft section, and every eleven seconds it swings past you.
recent.picture: View from a small salvage skiff cockpit with grapple arms visible: a huge ore freighter broken in half, slowly tumbling among glittering debris and dark asteroids in the deep asteroid belt, distant faint sunlight. A lean young man in his early twenties, short dark brown hair, light stubble, keen grey eyes, worn olive flight jacket over a grey t-shirt, at the controls, seen from behind.

recent.action: Scan the wreck before moving closer
recent.narration:
You hold the skiff at a safe distance and let the scanner sweep the wreck. The aft section's spin is steady, which is the only good news. The recorder bay hatch is buckled shut, so you'll need the cutting arm. A twisted hull plate the size of a hangar door is caught in the same tumble, and it sweeps across the bay a few seconds after the hatch passes.

The nav core is closer to the break, where torn cables drift loose.

That gives you about four seconds between the hatch and the plate. It's enough to grapple on, as long as you don't hesitate.

action: Match the spin and grapple the hatch
